daily.summary: The main development links last week's Norwegian energy incidents to a cloud flaw. Microsoft says an Azure API Management weakness exposed stored secrets, and Norway's NSM reportedly ties it to Equinor and Skagerak Energi. South Korea's power utility KEPCO disclosed a breach of its billing and procurement systems. CISA added exploited N-able Mail Assure and MONAI Label flaws to its KEV catalog, and the FBI crime database breach remains unexplained.

weekly.summary: AI-assisted intrusion remains the week's main theme: the FBI, Google, Unit 42 and Amazon describe autonomous attack frameworks in real operations, and Bell Canada and the European Commission say AI-driven attackers breached them. Energy operators feature prominently, with Norway reportedly linking Equinor and Skagerak Energi incidents to an exploited Azure API Management flaw and KEPCO disclosing a large data breach. State-linked activity includes a China-nexus vCenter zero-day campaign, Russian espionage against Romanian and US targets, and North Korean financial theft. Government breaches in Austria, West Virginia and at the FBI remain unattributed.
